thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 - `us-west-2` serving degradation (ELB 5xx spike + instance detaches) — paging sarah_oncall and mike_sre

incident-bot: Alert details: multiple ELB target group healthcheck failures in us-west-2a, increased 5xx rate across api-prod; Route53 weighted failover activated for some customers.

sarah_oncall: seeing 5xxs and high latencies on the dashboards, biggest from us-west-2a. ELB target group shows a lot of `unhealthy` then `initial` then `unhealthy` loops.

sarah_oncall: digging into instance logs now — I see a bunch of `eni detach` messages in the kernel log around the same time as 5xx flood.

mike_sre: i'm up, taking pager. can you paste the ELB TG name and any failing instance ids?

sarah_oncall: TG: prod-api-tg-usw2; failing ids: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h, i-0b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i (multiple repeated).

alex_platform: hitting the AWS console now — EC2 shows those instances with `impaired` network interfaces, CloudWatch for `ENIDetach` shows a short spike at 02:13 UTC.

jamie_prod: customer tickets rolling in — Support seeing errors for embed generation and streaming endpoints. Estimating ~12% of traffic affected, mostly traffic that routes to us-west-2a.

catie_support: escalating a VIP customer SLA impact to account team — they saw ~30% error rate for ~8 minutes. forwarding logs.

ops-runner: adding runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-eni-detach and https://redwood.internal/incidents/route53-failover-guides

sarah_oncall: logs show `EBS read timeout` on the same hosts just before ENI detach. Could be noisy IO causing kernel to reset NIC? Not sure yet.

mike_sre: two parallel hypotheses: 1) host-level EBS IO contention causing kernel watchdog resets -> ENI detach -> ELB bad; 2) AZ fabric causing ENI flapping. we need mitigation to reduce customer impact now.

alex_platform: Route53 is already running a weighted failover we had preconfigured — some traffic shifted to secondary weight in us-east-1. I can bump weight to 0 for us-west-2a if we want an immediate cutover. TTL is 30s.

jamie_prod: do it. customers are hitting endpoints now. prefer quick cutover + gradual failback after cleanups.

sarah_oncall: agree. do the Route53 weight shift to 0 for that az's record and set health check to failover? Also set ELB connection draining to 300s?

alex_platform: making the DNS change now: running:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1ABCDEF --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2a","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"34.200.1.12"}]}}]}'
```

alex_platform: change submitted, propagation should be quick due to low TTL. also pausing weighted traffic for us-west-2a.

incident-bot: Route53 change completed (change id: /change/C12345).

mike_sre: while DNS changes propagate, we should mark affected instances cordoned and spin up replacements in other AZs to catch steady-state load. sarah, can you initiate ASG replace for the failing instances?

sarah_oncall: kicking off ASG replace for prod-api-asg-usw2 with desired=+2 temporarily and draining the unhealthy instances from TG. using lifecycle hooks.

sarah_oncall: command:
```
aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh --auto-scaling-group-name prod-api-asg-usw2 --strategy Rolling --preferences '{"MinHealthyPercentage":50}'
```

ops-runner: NOTE: if we increase desired count, watch GPU-backed infer nodes — we have limits per AZ, ensure capacity is available.

alex_platform: capacity looks OK in other AZs. also setting ELB deregistration delay to 60s to speed turnover.

mike_sre: good. also open a support case with AWS for EBS/ENI correlation in us-west-2a. include instance ids and CloudTrail for ENIDetach events.

sarah_oncall: case opened: case #1234567890. AWS support acknowledged and says they're seeing elevated EBS latency in the AZ and are investigating.

jamie_prod: customer comms: posting to status page that we're experiencing regional degradation in us-west-2 due to underlying cloud storage/networking; routing traffic to healthy regions, mitigations in progress. ETA unknown.

catie_support: posting scheduled update to impacted customers now. will add note when AWS provides root cause.

mike_sre: i'm taking lead for incident, sarah you can hand off after you confirm replacement instances are healthy. I'll stay until AWS confirms or we fully fail back.

sarah_oncall: handing off to mike_sre — I validated new instances in other AZs registered healthy with TG, error rate dropped ~85% after DNS shift. last check 02:24 UTC.

mike_sre: thanks. continuing monitoring. next steps: 1) wait for AWS response on EBS/ENI correlation; 2) let instance refresh finish; 3) plan controlled failback once AWS confirms AZ stability and we see no ENIDetach.

incident-bot: page acknowledged by mike_sre. incident severity remains P1.

alex_platform: adding a short-term automation: if `ENIDetach` spike > 5 in 5m, auto-adjust Route53 weight to 0 for that set — flagging for postmortem discussion.

jamie_prod: agreed. also capture a reproducible eval harness to test traffic routing during failover for next sim.

catie_support: updating the ticket queue and tagging affected customer accounts.

mike_sre: logging timeline and actions in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3055556789 (will fill RCA after AWS reply).

incident-bot: Incident channel bridge created for on-call handoff to SE team.

mike_sre: closing this handoff — keeping the channel open for updates. if you see fresh ENI flaps post-03:00 UTC, ping me directly.

sarah_oncall: thanks — good handoff. I'll resume normal rotation. :white_check_mark:

ops-runner: postmortem checklist added to incident doc; root cause to be updated when AWS provides details.

jamie_prod: final note: customer impact summary to include per-customer error windows and any SLA credits.

mike_sre: acknowledged. will follow up with timeline and remediation items.
